round: V21: retrain late tables under official-modern rules; new stage for >=6144 (goal 12288)
rules: Official-modern (RULES.md): window-first bonus, 1/21, 12288 ends the game.
baseModel: training/v7/base.ntd (= dist/models/ntuple-v8.bin; its stage 1/2 tables equal the website V4 model). Loaded as four stages with stage 3 = copy of stage 2.
scopeChange: Stage 1 (1536-3072) is not retrained: under both rules 3072 is reached from 1536 in about 90% of games and a stage-1 effect cannot be measured cheaply. Stage 0 unchanged.

training.method: TD(lambda=.5), five-step truncated return, undiscounted future score (spawn + merge points), squared-multiplicity normalised updates, values recorded at play time. Behaviour: two-move score policy (as V2-V7). Episodes start from real snapshots with the unseen deck reshuffled.

S2.boundary: first 6144 afterstate bootstraps with the frozen stage-3 value (= old stage 2) and ends the episode

training.alphaSchedule: first value until 50% of CPU budget, second until 85%, third after
training.newModel: stage 0/1 from base, stage 2 from S2, stage 3 from S3 (four-stage file)

pools: make_pools.py: EVAL3072 = first 1024 first-3072 snapshots (openings 21110001+); EVAL6144 = first 512 first-6144 snapshots made by extending first-3072 snapshots of openings 21310001+ with 4-ply/0.003; TRAIN pools from openings 21510001+. Pools are disjoint by source seed. No filtering. evalA used openings 21110001-21111660 (1600 games gave 1023 first-3072 snapshots; 60 more games were added before any evaluation). Final sizes: EVAL3072 1024, EVAL6144 512, train-3072 781, train-6144 248. A temp-file bug in the first extension run could drop snapshots; all 6144 extensions were deleted and regenerated before any use. Correction before any NEW-model run: one first-6144 snapshot of evalB was already terminal (the 6144 appeared on the losing move, no decision left); terminal snapshots are excluded and EVAL6144 is the first 512 non-terminal ones (514 available). The extend tool now skips terminal states. Only CUR continuations for indices >= 128 were affected and were rerun.

evaluation.search: website default: 5-ply, cutoff 0.01, complete depth every move, native C++.
evaluation.pairing: Same snapshot and same rollout seed for both models (unseen deck reshuffled with seed base+index).

E1.compare: NEW vs CUR (differ only in stage 2 here)

E2.compare: NEW vs CUR (differ only in stage 3 here)
E2.endpoint: mean score gained after the snapshot; paired t-test
E2.secondary: reach a 3072 beside the 6144 (second-largest card rank >= 13), McNemar; number of 12288s; moves survived

multiplicity: Holm across the two primary endpoints (E1, E2).
interim: One interim look at 50% of each pool (Haybittle-Peto): stop that comparison early only if two-sided p < 0.001; otherwise run to completion and test at the final Holm level.
adoption: Each retrained table is adopted on its own if its primary endpoint is better after Holm; otherwise the current table for that stage is kept. Browser timing and JS/C++ parity are checked before any website change.
limits: Conditional on these snapshot distributions (3-ply to 3072, 4-ply cutoff to 6144); late-stage results are not whole-game rates. 12288 is expected to be rare, hence the continuous primary endpoint for E2.

frozenModels.note: hashes recorded before any NEW evaluation
